studying.howILearn: Through conversation. You teach; I call out what resonates and we follow that thread; along the way you name the few things worth remembering, and they stick. When we stop, save it: update the pages it touched (what resonated, what to remember), add any idea of mine as a concept, and add a learning-path entry if the inquiry changed direction.

pages.what: the question you’re actually trying to answer, what it’s for, and when you’ll know enough
each finding, how sure we are, and its sources

research.how: I may start with an approximate description, examples, or something that caught my attention. Help me locate the question I’m actually trying to answer. Begin broad enough to map the territory, then follow the strongest leads into specifics. Show me diagrams or maps when they make the relationships easier to see. Keep sources, findings, assumptions and disagreements distinct. Help me recognize when I know enough to use the answer, and what remains uncertain.
research.closeWhen: the answer is useful enough for its purpose, or what remains uncertain is clearly stated

pages.what: the idea in your own words, and how it has changed

idea.how: I may start with a hunch, an image or half a sentence. Help me say it in my own words, then show me what it could become — possibilities, tensions, objections. Keep my idea apart from what you add. Don’t turn it into a plan before I’m ready; when a direction appears, help me decide whether to research it, decide on it or start it.
idea.closeWhen: you choose a direction, set it aside, or turn it into other work

pages.what: the choice, the options, what matters most, who decides — and the decision, why, what it gives up and what would make you revisit it

decide.how: I usually start with the choice in front of me and a gut feeling. Help me lay out the options and what matters most, find what I don’t know yet, and hear the views that differ from mine. Keep what’s been proposed apart from what’s been decided. When I choose, record the reason, what I’m giving up, and what would make me revisit it.
decide.closeWhen: a choice is made, deferred, or rejected with a reason

pages.what: where you’re heading, what’s known, assumed and still open, the options, what’s chosen, and the path — order, timing, costs — with what would make you revisit it

plan.how: I may start with a fuzzy picture or with much already settled. See how far along it is and start there; don’t walk me through steps in order. Build the picture with me instead of asking for everything up front. Keep what’s known, assumed and decided apart. Ask the question that most changes the path next, and leave open what wouldn’t change it yet. Say when something needs research or a decision. When numbers depend on each other, like costs, keep them in a table I can check.
plan.closeWhen: the path is clear enough to start (it becomes an Initiative, keeping PLAN.md), or the plan is dropped

pages.what: what you’re trying to change, why, what’s in and out, and how you’ll know it’s done
what was chosen, who chose, why, and what would change it

initiative.how: I may start with a problem, a possibility, a request, or an outcome I want. Help me understand what is happening and who it affects. Bring in other perspectives where they matter, develop possible approaches, and help me choose what to try. Keep ideas and proposals separate from decisions. Record who actually accepted a commitment, what we did, what happened, and what still needs attention. Start wherever the work really is; I may need to revisit an earlier choice.
initiative.closeWhen: the outcome is achieved, abandoned, or handed into recurring work

pages.what: what normally happens, who handles each part, and what a good run looks like
what is watched, and what counts as normal

operation.how: Help me describe what normally happens, who handles each part, and what a good result looks like. As it repeats, focus on meaningful exceptions and patterns rather than writing up every ordinary run. When we consider changing the process, show the reason, the alternatives, who decides, and how we will tell whether the change helped. Keep the current process aligned with decisions that were actually made.
operation.closeWhen: the recurring work is retired or replaced

classifications.label: Decision
classifications.note: A decision was made, with the evidence behind it

classifications.label: Assumption
classifications.note: Taken as true, not yet tested

classifications.label: Known issue
classifications.note: A confirmed, stable problem or limitation

classifications.label: Method / how-to
classifications.note: How something should be done or analyzed

classifications.label: Fact from a source
classifications.note: A fact from a source — a spec sheet, a measurement, a document, a test result; without a source it is an assumption

classifications.label: Question / dispute
classifications.note: Someone questions a conclusion, number or record — still open ("are you sure?" counts)

classifications.label: Correction
classifications.note: An earlier statement was wrong; this replaces it. Fill supersedes: and mark the old record superseded

classifications.label: Interpretation
classifications.note: An interpretation or reasoning — not a sourced fact; list what it rests on in references: / source_refs:

classifications.label: Preference
classifications.note: How the owner wants output produced

neverSave: Passwords, API keys and other secrets
Personal medical records — diagnoses, test results, treatment
